description:

title: (CS)²AI Online™ Seminar: Cybersecurity in America’s Water Industry
description:
**[Cybersecurity in America’s Water Industry: Are We Asking the Right Questions?](https://events.zoom.us/ev/AkPBo5EIbae7MMI6sp_7_DbtWUCepxD72B4C_GnH5NJ9hEgzznbH~AncnAgItqTo8ABKl4FLamodjhI8T2q6Yo_9QFzRjv6CF-h0IcHqRO4ZgfIgV8JTzbIUx27JBkRaZe8OiIYZubuvI1w)**

Cybersecurity threats to America’s water and wastewater systems continue to evolve, exposing vulnerabilities in an industry that provides essential services but often operates with limited resources. While awareness of cyber risks is growing, are utilities focusing on the right priorities?

This presentation examines the current state of cybersecurity in the US water sector, drawing on recent incidents to highlight
the real-world operational consequences of cyberattacks. It challenges conventional approaches to cybersecurity, emphasizing the importance of understanding operational risks, implementing practical and proportionate security measures, and preparing for incidents before they occur. Drawing on ISA/IEC 62443 and industry best practices, the session explores the questions utilities should be asking to move beyond compliance and build genuine operational resilience.

**Your journey into innovation starts here! ☄️**
Join **The AI Collective Hampton Roads** for *The Launchpad*, the opening event of **The Next Frontier 2026**, a community-driven space innovation hackathon where science, technology, and creativity collide.

title: The Next Frontier | Mission Control
description:
# 🚀 Mission Control: Pitch, Explore & Collaborate

**Bring your curiosity. Share your ideas. Find your crew. ☄️**
Welcome to **Mission Control**, the official kickoff of **The Next Frontier 2026**, a community-driven space innovation hackathon hosted by AI Collective Hampton Roads!
This is where ideas begin to take shape.
Have an idea for an app, scientific research tool, AI project, or creative solution? Maybe you've identified a problem but aren't sure how to solve it. Or perhaps you're simply curious about science and technology and want to explore what's possible.
**You don't need a polished pitch, a finished concept, or even a team to participate!**
During this interactive kickoff, we'll:

* 🚀 **Pitch Our Rough Ideas:** Share early concepts, scientific questions, or problems you'd love to solve.
* 💡 **Brainstorm Together:** Bounce ideas off fellow innovators, exchange perspectives, and discover possibilities you might not have considered.
* 🤝 **Find Your Crew:** Meet potential collaborators with complementary skills, interests, and expertise.
* 🔭 **Explore the Challenge:** Learn about The Next Frontier's mission, project expectations, resources, and opportunities.
* 🛠️ **Prepare to Build:** Refine your concept, identify next steps, and leave with a clearer direction for your project.

Whether you're a student, scientist, developer, designer, entrepreneur, or someone who simply loves asking questions, there's a place for you at Mission Control.
**The goal isn't to arrive with the perfect idea. It's to discover what your idea could become through collaboration.**

title: WSDG November Technical Presentation
description:
Detection and Notification Case Studies
by Glover Barker

Abstract:
An overview will be provided of three different domains in which a system is monitored for problems and the user is notified, and the user must respond. Commonalities and differences will be discussed. The domains are: Network Malware Filtering and Scanning, Airport Traffic Conflict Detection, and Intravenous Infiltration Monitoring.

Bio:
Glover Barker is a retired Software Architect. His background includes software development in C++, Python, and various other languages. He has also worked in management, requirements, design, testing, quality assurance, and configuration management. Past companies include ivWatch, NASA contractors, Symantec, R. R. Donnelley, Reuters, and AT&T Bell Laboratories.

title: Code + Coffee | Cafe Stella
description:
Join us for a relaxed morning meetup where developers, designers, founders, and tech enthusiasts gather over great coffee to talk shop, share ideas, and connect with others in the local tech community.

**Code + Coffee** has no formal agenda—just bring your laptop, a project you’re working on, a question you’ve been thinking about, or simply come to meet other people building interesting things. Whether you're coding, designing, experimenting with AI, launching a startup, or just curious about technology, you'll find friendly conversations and plenty of inspiration.

Expect:

* Good coffee
* Interesting technical conversations
* People sharing projects and ideas
* Occasional spontaneous whiteboard sessions

Drop in anytime during the meetup window.

Stay for 10 minutes or the whole time.

If you’ve been looking for a low-key way to meet other developers in the area, this is it.

**Cafe Stella** has a policy that requires a purchase if you're sitting and staying in their space. Always a good idea to support the establishments we visit regardless.

### **Moved to Tap It Local in Chesapeake**

## **Attention Information Security and Cybersecurity Professionals!**

Are you looking to meet new people who share your interests? Whether you're considering a career in cybersecurity, just getting started, or are a seasoned professional, we welcome everyone for an evening of networking, learning, and great conversation.

Join us at **Tap-It Local** in Chesapeake for a relaxed evening of networking with fellow IT and cybersecurity professionals.
